scenario.domain_notes: AI data hall fit-out. New racks go in rows under the busways. Each rack needs a cdu and a busway assignment. Busways: continuous load <= capacity_kw*derate. CDUs: assigned load <= capacity_kw, total load must survive loss of the largest CDU (N+1), hose run (Manhattan distance rack center -> CDU port) <= hose_m. Racks in the same row abut (gap 0); aisles between rows >= 1.2 m. Keepouts and egress corridors must stay clear.

spec.interpretation: Deploy 16 GB200 NVL72 racks (132 kW each, 2.1 MW) in rows under the busways, every rack on a CDU loop and a busway tap, with N+1 cooling and all code zones clear.
assumptions: 16 racks x 132 kW = 2,112 kW meets the 2 MW goal.
Racks in a row abut; aisles are at least 1.2 m.
Hose runs are Manhattan distance to the CDU port.
Busways carry at most 80% of rating continuously.

checks.why: mandatory: physical collisions are never acceptable
mandatory: the layout must fit the floor
mandatory: structural elements are immovable
The goal is 2 MW of IT load.
Each CDU can only reject the heat of the racks on its loop (800 kW).
Busway continuous load must stay within 80% of its 800 kW rating.

source.title: NFPA 70 (NEC): continuous loads and the 80% rule
source.snippet: Paraphrase: size feeders so continuous load stays at or below 80% of the overcurrent device rating.

checks.why: N+1 cooling: losing the largest CDU must not overheat any rack.

Tap-box whips reach 0.8 m, so every rack must sit under its busway.
Hot and cold aisles need 1.2 m for service carts.
